builds.analysis_root_cause: The test 'Should create a management cluster and then upgrade all the providers' failed at 10:39:01 UTC when clusterctl upgrade apply timed out after approximately 5 minutes (build-log.txt the cited artifact evidence: '[FAILED] in [It] - / @ 07/26/26 10:39:01.593'). The upgrade was invoked at the cited artifact evidence as 'clusterctl upgrade apply ... v1beta2'. The terminal error from build-log.txt the cited artifact evidence/1824 is: 'failed to list objects for the "network.azure.com/v1api20201101, Kind=VirtualNetworksSubnet" GroupVersionKind: action failed after 9 attempts: client rate limiter Wait returned an error: context deadline exceeded'. The causal chain is fully documented in artifacts/clusters/clusterctl-upgrade-management-atup1n/clusterctl-upgrade.log: line 17 shows 'Scaling down Provider={"name":"infrastructure-azure","namespace":"capz-system"} providerVersion="v1.26.0"'; line 18 shows 'Scaling down Deployment={"name":"azureserviceoperator-controller-manager","namespace":"capz-system"}'; line 19 shows 'Retrying with backoff cause="Deployment still has 2 replicas"'; line 20 shows 'Scaling down Deployment={"name":"capz-controller-manager","namespace":"capz-system"}'; line 26 shows 'Deleting Service="azureserviceoperator-webhook-service" Namespace="capz-system"'; lines 42-45 show deletion of azureserviceoperator-validating-webhook-configuration, capz-validating-webhook-configuration, azureserviceoperator-mutating-webhook-configuration, and capz-mutating-webhook-configuration. After the ASO controller manager was scaled down and its webhook service and webhook configurations were deleted, clusterctl attempted to enumerate all custom resources owned by the old provider — including ASO-managed multi-version CRDs such as network.azure.com/v1api20201101 VirtualNetworksSubnet. Because the Kubernetes API server must call the ASO conversion webhook to serve objects stored in a non-hub version, and the azureserviceoperator-webhook-service no longer existed, every API list call for ASO GVKs was refused. The client-side rate-limiter backed off across 9 attempts until context deadline was exceeded. The root cause is that ASO-managed CRDs were not labeled with cluster.x-k8s.io/provider=infrastructure-azure before upgrade, so clusterctl tore down the ASO webhook service while it still needed it for CRD object conversion during resource discovery. This is a code-level ordering bug, not a transient infrastructure flake: the webhook was deliberately deleted by clusterctl before the list operations that depend on it had completed.

builds.analysis_root_cause: During the clusterctl upgrade on management cluster `clusterctl-upgrade-management-g9706x`, the upgrade sequence scales down the old CAPI core provider (line 33 of `artifacts/clusters/clusterctl-upgrade-management-g9706x/clusterctl-upgrade.log`: `Deleting Provider={"name":"cluster-api","namespace":"capi-system"} providerVersion="v1.12.10"`). Immediately after, clusterctl enumerates resources owned by the infrastructure provider, including the ASO-managed GVK `containerservice.azure.com/v1api20230201, Kind=ManagedClustersAgentPool`. Listing objects of that CRD requires a Kubernetes API conversion webhook call to `azureserviceoperator-webhook-service.capz-system.svc:443` to convert them to the stored version `containerservice.azure.com/v1api20250801storage`. Because the CAPZ/ASO provider was scaled down as part of the upgrade, the webhook pod is no longer available. Line 34 of the same log shows the root error: `storage is (re)initializing: failed to list containerservice.azure.com/v1api20230201, Kind=ManagedClustersAgentPool: conversion webhook for containerservice.azure.com/v1api20250801storage, Kind=ManagedClustersAgentPool failed: Post "https://azureserviceoperator-webhook-service.capz-system.svc:443/convert?timeout=30s": dial tcp 10.102.172.24:443: connect: connection refused`. All 8 subsequent retries (the cited artifact evidence of the same log) hit the client-side rate-limiter deadline: `client rate limiter Wait returned an error: context deadline exceeded`. After exhausting 9 total attempts the test fails, as confirmed in `build-log.txt` (grep match at the cited artifact evidence): `failed to list objects for the "containerservice.azure.com/v1api20230201, Kind=ManagedClustersAgentPool" GroupVersionKind: action failed after 9 attempts: client rate limiter Wait returned an error: context deadline exceeded`. The failure is at `` (build-log.txt the cited artifact evidence). This is not Azure ARM throttling — no HTTP 429 or RateLimitExceeded appears in any artifact; the rate-limiter error is purely client-side queue saturation caused by repeated failed conversion webhook calls after the ASO webhook pod was terminated. The tested revision is CAPZ `5f12ddee9a6f7b79c1180c5a6d5e07b8dcde2e63` on branch main (started.json). The underlying cause is a provider lifecycle ordering bug: ASO-managed CRDs requiring multi-version conversion are enumerated by clusterctl after the ASO webhook deployment has already been terminated, with no pre-upgrade step to label those CRDs with `cluster.x-k8s.io/provider=infrastructure-azure` so clusterctl can handle them before provider scale-down.

builds.analysis_root_cause: The CAPZ e2e wrapper runs the Kubernetes conformance suite inside a container (gcr.io/k8s-staging-ci-images/conformance:v1.38.0-alpha.0.6_94c136764292cc) via kubetest. The container exited with code 1 because exactly one test failed inside the suite (artifacts/junit.kubetest.9n4msz6f69.01.xml, line 2: failures="1"). The failing test was '[sig-node] [DRA] [FeatureGate:DRAExtendedResource] [Feature:DynamicResourceAllocation] must run pods with extended resource on dra nodes and device plugin nodes [KubeletMinVersion:1.35] [Serial]' (JUnit the cited artifact evidence). Its failure message reads: 'start pod1: Timed out after 300.000s. Expected Pod to be in <v1.PodPhase>: Running'. The pod was successfully scheduled and got Calico CNI annotations (cni.projectcalico.org/podIP: 192.168.201.65/32), but never transitioned to Running within the 300-second timeout. This is a test-level failure in the DRA extended-resource combined device-plugin scenario, not a CAPZ infrastructure failure — the cluster itself was healthy (all 3213 other tests were passed or skipped, and the control plane came up successfully at 20:39 per build-log.txt the cited artifact evidence). The outer CAPZ test then caught the non-zero container exit and reported it as 'Unable to run conformance tests: error container run failed with exit code 1' (artifacts/junit.e2e_suite.1.xml).

The CAPZ e2e conformance wrapper ran the Kubernetes DRA e2e suite (gcr.io/k8s-staging-ci-images/conformance:v1.38.0-alpha.0.6_94c136764292cc) with label-filter 'DRA && Feature: isSubsetOf { OffByDefault, DynamicResourceAllocation } && !Alpha && !Flaky'. Of 113 specs, 112 passed and 1 failed (build-log.txt the cited artifact evidence). The sole failing spec is '[sig-node] [DRA] [FeatureGate:DRAExtendedResource] [Feature:DynamicResourceAllocation] [It] must run pods with extended resource on dra nodes and device plugin nodes [KubeletMinVersion:1.35] [FeatureGate:DynamicResourceAllocation] [Serial]' at  (build-log.txt the cited artifact evidence). The stack trace at build-log.txt the cited artifact evidence shows the failure was in 'pod.WaitTimeoutForPodRunningInNamespace', i.e., a pod never reached Running. The pod's status dump at lines ~43571-43575 shows it requested 'example.com/resource: "2"' as both a limit and a request with startTime '2026-08-10T02:55:17Z', yet never became Running before the 5-minute framework timeout fired at 03:00:17 (build-log.txt the cited artifact evidence: 'Failed inside E2E framework'). This test exercises the DRAExtendedResource feature gate interaction between a DRA driver and a device plugin advertising the same extended resource; the pod being stuck after scheduling indicates the device plugin was not fulfilling the 'example.com/resource' allocation, or the DRA+device-plugin combined allocation path failed silently. CAPZ infrastructure was not the cause: the control plane Machine was Running, both worker MachinePool nodes provisioned successfully, and 112 other DRA tests passed on the same cluster. The e2e suite exit code 1 propagated to the CAPZ wrapper, producing 'Unable to run conformance tests: error container run failed with exit code 1' (build-log.txt line 77824).

The cluster was provisioned successfully: the control-plane Machine `capz-conf-51theo-control-plane-xc7w7` reached phase Running with all conditions True (artifacts/clusters/bootstrap/resources/capz-conf-51theo/Machine/capz-conf-51theo-control-plane-xc7w7.yaml, status.phase=Running, NodeHealthy=True). The worker node `capz-conf-51theo-mp-0000000` was also Ready with ProviderID set (artifacts/clusters/capz-conf-51theo/nodes/capz-conf-51theo-mp-0000000/node-describe.txt, line 39: `Ready True ... KubeletReady`; the cited artifact evidence: ProviderID=`azure:///...capz-conf-51theo-mp-0/virtualMachines/0`). However, the same node-describe.txt shows `example.com/resource: 0` in both Capacity and Allocatable (the cited artifact evidence and 54), and `example.com/resource 0 0` in Allocated resources (the cited artifact evidence). This means the device plugin responsible for advertising `example.com/resource` did not register any resource units on the node. The DRA test `[sig-node] [DRA] [FeatureGate:DRAExtendedResource] must run pods with extended resource on dra nodes and device plugin nodes [Serial]` (artifacts/junit.kubetest.k9wt5wc65b.01.xml, the single failing testcase) requires a pod to consume both a DRA-allocated extended resource and a device-plugin-advertised extended resource simultaneously. Because `example.com/resource` capacity was 0, the scheduler could not satisfy the device-plugin resource claim for pod2, and the pod remained pending/non-Running until the 300s timeout. The outer CAPZ conformance wrapper then reported `error container run failed with exit code 1`.

cases.root_cause: The DRA test '[sig-node] [DRA] [FeatureGate:DRAExtendedResource] must run pods with extended resource on dra nodes and device plugin nodes' fails because the `example.com/resource` device plugin endpoint is not available in kubelet's device plugin cache at the time pods are scheduled. In build 2086549231711031296 and 2086635048097812480, the test does not wait for the sample-device-plugin-beta DaemonSet pod to fully start and register `example.com/resource` with kubelet before scheduling tester pods, resulting in 'CreateContainerConfigError: endpoint not found in cache for a registered resource: example.com/resource' and a 300s pod-start timeout. In build 2086801898869886976, `example.com/resource` capacity was 0 in both Capacity and Allocatable on the worker node, indicating the device plugin never successfully advertised any resource units, similarly preventing the scheduler from satisfying the device-plugin resource claim. All three failures share the same root mechanism: the legacy device plugin serving `example.com/resource` is not ready/registered in kubelet's cache when the test attempts to run pods requiring that resource.

builds.analysis_root_cause: The test 'Creating a highly-available cluster with Azure Linux 3' provisioned cluster capz-e2e-0hycdy-azl3 (Kubernetes v1.35.6, azl3 flavor, 3 control-plane machines). The first CP node initialized successfully and all addons (cloud-provider-azure, Calico CNI, azuredisk-csi-driver) deployed and became available by 11:21:42 UTC (build-log.txt the cited artifact evidence). The test then waited for all 3 control-plane nodes to exist starting at 11:22:13 UTC (build-log.txt the cited artifact evidence). The second joining CP machine capz-e2e-0hycdy-azl3-control-plane-c45tj successfully passed all kubeadm preflight checks, resolved the API server hostname (capz-e2e-0hycdy-azl3-da35c390.switzerlandnorth.cloudapp.azure.com:6443), fetched the cluster-info ConfigMap and kubeadm-config, retrieved TLS bootstrap credentials, validated all certificates (CA, front-proxy CA, etcd CA), confirmed all images present (e.g. 'image exists: registry.k8s.io/kube-apiserver:v1.35.6'), and validated etcd directory emptiness — no preKubeadmCommands errors, no download failures, no configuration errors, no image pull failures are present in boot.log. Then at 11:21:49 UTC it attempted `[etcd] Adding etcd member: https://10.0.0.5:2380` (boot.log line ~1283) and immediately failed: 'error: error execution phase etcd-join: error creating local etcd static pod manifest file: context deadline exceeded' (boot.log lines ~1283-1284). Cloud-init then reported scripts-user module failure and exited. No further kubeadm join retry occurred on this node. Because this node never joined etcd, KCP was blocked: the clusterctl describe output (clusterctl-describe-cluster-capz-e2e-0hycdy-azl3.txt) shows 'Scaling up from 2 to 3 replicas is blocked because: * waiting for control plane components to become healthy * waiting for etcd cluster to become healthy', and Machine capz-e2e-0hycdy-azl3-control-plane-c45tj is stuck with 'NodeHealthy: Waiting for a Node with spec.providerID ... to exist'. The test framework WaitForAllControlPlaneNodesToExist () timed out after 3600s at 12:22:13 UTC with 'Expected <int>: 1 to equal <int>: 3'. The boot.log for c45tj shows no upstream cause preceding the etcd-join failure — all checks passed cleanly — confirming this is the classic transient etcd member-add timing flake with no specific bootstrap or code defect.

builds.analysis_root_cause: The test 'Creating a highly-available cluster with Azure Linux 3' timed out (build-log.txt the cited artifact evidence) after waiting 60 minutes for 3 control-plane nodes to exist; only 2 existed. The KCP resource (artifacts/clusters/bootstrap/resources/capz-e2e-wimt1f/KubeadmControlPlane/capz-e2e-wimt1f-azl3-control-plane.yaml) shows readyReplicas=2, replicas=3, with condition EtcdClusterHealthy=False: '2 of 3 etcd members are healthy, 1 learner etcd member' and ControlPlaneComponentsHealthy=Unknown: 'Waiting for a Node with spec.providerID ... capz-e2e-wimt1f-azl3-control-plane-2c2n7 to exist'. The Machine resource for the stuck node (artifacts/clusters/bootstrap/resources/capz-e2e-wimt1f/Machine/capz-e2e-wimt1f-azl3-control-plane-2c2n7.yaml) shows InfrastructureReady=True (13:22:52) and phase=Provisioned, but NodeHealthy=Unknown: 'Waiting for a Node with spec.providerID ... to exist' since 13:16:56 — meaning the VM was running but kubelet never registered a Node object. The AzureMachine (artifacts/clusters/bootstrap/resources/capz-e2e-wimt1f/AzureMachine/capz-e2e-wimt1f-azl3-control-plane-2c2n7.yaml) confirms VMRunning=True and BootstrapSucceeded=True. The third node joined etcd as a learner (indicating kubeadm join partially executed) but the kubelet never successfully registered. Log collection from the node also failed: 'dialing from control plane to target node at capz-e2e-wimt1f-azl3-control-plane-2c2n7: ssh: rejected: connect failed (Temporary failure in name resolution)' (build-log.txt line 5379). All per-node logs (cloud-init-output.log, kubelet.log, journal.log) are 0 bytes, so no concrete bootstrap-level failure (preKubeadmCommands error, package failure, cert error) can be confirmed. The boot.log (345 KB, unread due to budget) may contain more detail. The pattern — VM running, etcd learner stuck, kubelet never registering, no concrete upstream cause in reachable logs — matches the known transient etcd-join / API-server unreachable timeout class for joining control-plane nodes.

builds.analysis_root_cause: The test 'Creating a highly-available cluster with Azure Linux 3' deployed Kubernetes v1.35.6 with 3 control-plane machines (build-log.txt the cited artifact evidence: 'Creating the workload cluster with name "capz-e2e-g2223d-azl3" using the "azl3" template (Kubernetes v1.35.6, 3 control-plane machines, 2 worker machines)'). The first control-plane node initialized successfully and all addons (Calico, CCM, CSI) became available by 21:25:47 UTC (build-log.txt the cited artifact evidence: 'Deployment kube-system/csi-azuredisk-controller is now available'). The test then entered 'Waiting for all control plane nodes to exist' (build-log.txt the cited artifact evidence) and timed out 60 minutes later at 22:25:47 UTC (build-log.txt the cited artifact evidence: '[FAILED] in [It] - '). The KubeadmControlPlane resource (artifacts/clusters/bootstrap/resources/capz-e2e-g2223d/KubeadmControlPlane/capz-e2e-g2223d-azl3-control-plane.yaml) confirmed 'Scaling up control plane to 3 replicas (actual 2)' with readyReplicas: 2 and unavailableReplicas: 1. The third control-plane Machine capz-e2e-g2223d-azl3-control-plane-qhcnx remained in phase 'Provisioned' (artifacts/clusters/bootstrap/resources/capz-e2e-g2223d/Machine/capz-e2e-g2223d-azl3-control-plane-qhcnx.yaml). The machine's cloud-init-output.log was 0 bytes (no content). The boot.log (artifacts/clusters/capz-e2e-g2223d-azl3/machines/capz-e2e-g2223d-azl3-control-plane-qhcnx/boot.log) showed the VM booted cleanly, kubeadm successfully registered the node as an etcd learner ('Updated etcd member list: [{capz-e2e-g2223d-azl3-control-plane-qhcnx https://10.0.0.6:2380} {capz-e2e-g2223d-azl3-control-plane-t5p6g https://10.0.0.4:2380} {capz-e2e-g2223d-azl3-control-plane-7wkfv https://10.0.0.5:2380}]'), but then failed with 'error: error execution phase etcd-join: error creating local etcd static pod manifest file: context deadline exceeded'. No preKubeadmCommands errors, package failures, certificate issues, or configuration problems preceded this failure in the boot.log. The CAAPH controller log showed only normal cleanup reconciliation for the capz-e2e-g2223d namespace. The Azure activity logs for the azl3 cluster showed no VM provisioning failures. This matches the known transient 'etcd-join context deadline exceeded' class: the joining node was admitted as a learner but could not complete membership promotion within the deadline, with no specific upstream cause in any bootstrap artifact.

cases.root_cause: HA cluster creation with Azure Linux 3 (azl3) flavor timed out waiting for 3 control-plane nodes to exist because the third (or second) joining control-plane node's kubeadm join partially completed — the VM booted and passed preflight checks, but the etcd-join phase failed (either 'context deadline exceeded' creating the etcd static pod manifest, or the kubelet never registered a Node object after etcd learner promotion), leaving the KubeadmControlPlane stuck at readyReplicas=2 of 3.
